info.title: Campbooks API
info.description: The Campbooks HTTP API. Errors are RFC 9457 `application/problem+json`. Operations require an OAuth 2.1 bearer token with the scope they list (401 without a valid token, 403 without the scope) unless they are public. The `/bff/*` operations serve the web app only: they authenticate with its session cookie instead of a token.

get.description:
A Server-Sent Events stream of what changed in the workspace, for clients
that keep a cache: each `change` frame names a record and an operation
(`{"cursor","record":{"type","id"},"op":"upsert"|"delete","version"}`),
never its contents; refetch what you show. Frames: `ready` (where the
stream starts), `change`, `heartbeat` (an SSE comment, or the cursor when
it moved past changes you may not see), `reset` (your cursor is unknown,
expired or too far behind: refetch everything, continue from the
cursor given), `revoked` (you no longer belong to the workspace) and
`closing` (the stream ends; reconnect with your cursor). Every frame
that carries a cursor sets the SSE `id`, so `EventSource` resumes on its
own. You only receive changes of records a read operation you hold a
scope for returns.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: The last cursor received; resumes after it.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
The last cursor received, for clients that cannot send
`Last-Event-ID` (the header wins when both are present). Omit it to
start from now.

get.summary: Read from the API as the signed-in user.
get.description:
`/bff/api/<path>` is `/api/<path>` (same method, query, headers and
 body) with the session's access token attached, refreshed first when
 it is about to expire. The token never leaves the server. Answers are
 the API's own; without a live session the answer is 401
 `session_required` (sign in at `/bff/login`). POST, PUT, PATCH and
 DELETE need the `X-Campbooks-CSRF: 1` header from the app's origin.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The API path after `/api/`, e.g. `v1/system/version`; may contain slashes.

200.description: The API's response, whatever its status.

403.description: `csrf_check_failed`

503.description: `bff_not_configured`, or the identity provider is unavailable while the access token needs refreshing.

post.description:
Called by the identity provider, not browsers, when a user's IdP session
ends: ends the web sessions the signed logout token names (by IdP session
id, or every session of the user).

200.description: The sessions named by the token are ended.

503.description: `bff_not_configured`, or the identity provider's keys are unavailable.

get.description:
The identity provider redirects here. Checks that `state` names a sign-in
this browser started (single use), exchanges the code with the PKCE
verifier, validates the ID token (issuer, audience, nonce, expiry,
signature), starts a session and sets the `SameSite=Strict` session
cookie. Answers with a small same-origin page that moves on to
`return_to`: a browser treats the whole redirect chain from the IdP as
cross-site and would not send the new cookie on a plain redirect.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: The `state` sent with the authorization request.

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: An error code instead of a code.

200.description: Signed in; the page moves on to `return_to`.

503.description: `bff_not_configured`, or the identity provider is unreachable.

get.description:
Creates a short-lived sign-in (state, nonce, PKCE verifier) bound to this
browser by a `SameSite=Lax` login cookie, and redirects to the identity
provider's authorization endpoint.

parameters.name: return_to
parameters.description: Where to land after signing in: a path on this site (default `/`).

503.description: `bff_not_configured`, or the identity provider is unreachable.

post.description:
Ends the session, revokes its refresh token at the identity provider and
clears the cookie. Navigate to `logout_url` to end the identity
provider's session too.

200.description: Signed out (also when there was no session).

signup_code.description:
The signup code, when the instance's policy is `code` and this is the
caller's first workspace.

accept_url.description:
The link that accepts it (it carries the token). Returned only here,
once: no other endpoint, log or event ever shows it.

CreatedInvitation.description: A new invitation, as the inviter sees it once: with the link to pass on.

database.description: Database status; always `ok` in a 200 response.

status.description: Overall status; always `ok` in a 200 response.

InvitationList.description: Pending (not yet accepted) invitations, expired ones included.

InvitationView.description:
A pending invitation, as owners and admins see it. Never carries the
token.

role.description: The role they get on accepting.

email.description:
Their email address; the invitation can only be accepted by a user
whose verified email is this one.

role.description:
The role they get: `admin` or `member` (the default). Owners are made
by promotion, never by invitation.

LogoutResponse.description: Where to send the browser to sign out of the identity provider too.

logout_url.description:
The identity provider's end-session URL (RP-initiated logout), which
comes back to the app's root; `null` when it has none.

MemberList.description: The members, in the order they joined.

display_name.description: Their name, as their identity provider gives it.

email.description: Their email address, as their identity provider gives it.

Phase.description: Where a stream is in its reading.

code.description:
Stable machine-readable reason (`not_found`, `invalid_token`,
`last_owner`, …); the same in every locale. Match on this, never on
`title` or `detail`.

detail.description: What went wrong in this occurrence, in the request's locale.

title.description:
Short summary of the problem type, in the request's locale
(`Content-Language`).

type.description:
URI identifying the problem type; `about:blank` when the HTTP status
says it all.

example.detail: This resource does not exist, or you cannot see it.
example.title: Not found

SecurityEventView.description: One entry of the security log.

metadata.description: Ids and roles involved; never secrets.

SessionInfo.description: Who is signed in. Never contains a token.

authenticated.description: Whether the request carries a live session.

expires_at.description: When the session ends at the latest (it ends sooner if left unused).

SessionUser.description: The signed-in user, as the identity provider describes them.

sub.description: Stable user id at the identity provider.

capabilities.description: The capabilities to ask for (`messages` is offered today).

oneOf.description:
An existing connection of yours to extend (incremental consent);
the same account must consent.

expires_at.description: When the consent must be completed by.

StreamView.description: A change stream as the API shows it.

last_change_at.description: When a run last found a change.

paused.description: Paused until the member connects again.

phase.description: Where it is in its reading.

streams.description: How many streams will run now.

UpdateWorkspace.description: The settings to change; absent fields stay as they are.

commit.description: Git commit the build came from, when known (`GIT_SHA` at runtime).

purge_after.description: When its records will be purged for good.

WorkspaceList.description: The caller's workspaces, oldest first, each with their role.

WorkspaceView.description: A workspace, as its members see it.

oneOf.description: The caller's role in it; absent for a client token.

bearer.description:
An OAuth 2.1 access token (a JWT) issued by this instance's identity provider, the issuer configured as `CAMPBOOKS_AUTH__ISSUER`. Each operation lists the scope it requires; operations with an empty requirement are public. Scopes:

- `connectors:read`: See the outside accounts connected to your workspaces and how their sync is doing.
- `connectors:write`: Connect outside accounts (such as Gmail), sync them now and disconnect them.
- `system:read`: Read operational status.
- `workspaces:admin`: Manage workspaces you own or administer: settings, members, invitations, deletion and the security log.
- `workspaces:read`: See your workspaces and who belongs to them.
- `workspaces:write`: Create workspaces, accept invitations and leave workspaces.

session.name: __Host-campbooks_session
session.description: The web app's session cookie, set by `/bff/callback` (`HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Strict`; named `campbooks_session` when the instance's public URL is plain http). Unsafe methods also need the `X-Campbooks-CSRF: 1` header and a same-origin request.

tags.name: workspaces
tags.description: Workspaces, members and roles, invitations and the security log. Workspace-owned resources live under `/api/v1/w/{workspace_id}/`; a caller who is not a member (or a client token bound to another workspace) gets 404.

tags.name: connectors
tags.description: Connections to outside accounts (Gmail first): connect with the provider's consent, see their health, sync now, disconnect. Credentials are never returned.

tags.name: changes
tags.description: The change feed: a Server-Sent Events stream per workspace of the records that changed (ids only), so clients refetch only what they show.

tags.name: bff
tags.description: The web app's backend-for-frontend: sign-in, the session cookie and same-origin API access. Browsers only; other clients call `/api/*` with their own OAuth token.
